Acuity.why: Acuity sells Distech DDC and PLC controllers into hyperscaler data centers (Acuity Intelligent Spaces) and data-center lighting, including a purpose-built Lithonia Lighting BLT data-center luminaire (Acuity Brands Lighting), so data-center build-outs add controls and lighting sales; the CEO said it had a very strong year in data centers in fiscal 2026 for lighting and is in the door with more and more hyperscalers.
Acuity.evidence: Acuity Q4 FY2026 (10-01-2026), CEO Neil Ashe: 'We have the premier DDC controller in the market at Distech, and we've added a PLC controller, which puts us in position to service multiple hyperscalers going forward. And those discussions - the existing sales continue and are growing, as you would expect, and we are in the door with more and more hyperscalers over time.' Also: 'we had a very strong year in data centers in '26 for lighting. We introduced ... a purpose-built solution for data centers going forward.'

players.product: Distech DDC controller and PLC controller for hyperscaler data centers; data-center lighting (Lithonia Lighting BLT purpose-built data-center luminaire)

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 FY2026 results (CFO Karen Holcom): net sales $1.2 billion, $35 million or 3% above the prior year, driven by growth in Acuity Intelligent Spaces (AIS) and partially offset by revenue declines at Acuity Brands Lighting (ABL). Adjusted gross profit margin improved to 50.2%, up 130 basis points; both adjusted margins benefited from AIS becoming a larger part of the company. Adjusted operating profit $233 million, up $8 million or 3%, adjusted operating profit margin 18.7% (up 10 basis points); adjusted diluted EPS $5.77, up $0.57 or 11%, mainly from higher profitability and lower diluted shares outstanding. CEO Neil Ashe: AIS is now one-quarter of the business.
quarterly_data.figure: Net sales $1.2 billion (+3%); adjusted gross margin 50.2%; adjusted operating profit $233 million (margin 18.7%); adjusted diluted EPS $5.77 (+11%)

quarterly_data.signal: Acuity Brands Lighting (ABL) Q4 FY2026 (CFO Karen Holcom): sales $959 million, down $3 million or less than 1% versus Q4 FY2025, when ABL was working through an elevated backlog from orders accelerated ahead of price increases in the back half of fiscal 2025; on a two-year stacked basis total ABL sales were flat and the independent sales network and direct sales network combined grew 3%. Adjusted gross profit margin 46.2%, driven largely by product and productivity improvements; adjusted operating profit declined $14 million to $180 million, margin 18.8% (down 130 basis points) as ABL invested in technology. $32 million of tariff refunds and a $15 million special charge for productivity actions (product portfolio, supply chain, operating footprint) were adjusted out. CEO Neil Ashe: the charge mainly reflects adjusting the manufacturing network - one facility closed and consolidated into another - plus eliminating some smaller brands and product lines; Acuity expects to keep rationalizing its footprint as productivity improves. CEO: the higher Q4 ABL SG&A reflects timing and one-time items and will normalize.
quarterly_data.figure: ABL sales $959 million (down less than 1%); adjusted gross margin 46.2%; adjusted operating profit $180 million (margin 18.8%); tariff refunds $32 million; special charge $15 million

quarterly_data.signal: Acuity Intelligent Spaces (AIS) Q4 FY2026 (CFO Karen Holcom): sales $298 million, up $43 million or 17%, driven by strong growth across its portfolios; adjusted gross profit margin 61.2%, up 200 basis points; adjusted operating profit $74 million, up $19 million or 36%, adjusted operating profit margin 24.9% (up 350 basis points). $13 million of tariff refunds and a $3 million special charge for a facility impairment were adjusted out. CEO Neil Ashe: AIS has grown from about $150 million in revenue and negative operating income to a large, growing business, mostly organically but also through acquisitions; its businesses already carry high gross margins (high 50s, 60%) and operating margin improves as they scale.
quarterly_data.figure: AIS sales $298 million (+17%); adjusted gross margin 61.2%; adjusted operating profit $74 million (+36%, margin 24.9%)

quarterly_data.signal: FY2027 outlook (CFO Karen Holcom): net sales of $4.7 billion to $4.9 billion for total AYI, assuming ABL delivers flat to low single-digit sales growth and AIS low- to mid-teens sales growth; adjusted diluted EPS of $20.50 to $22. CEO Neil Ashe: the ABL guide assumes the lighting market is flat to down low single digits, with ABL taking share, increasing penetration of new verticals and adding corporate-accounts performance; ABL gross margin should keep improving from structural changes despite the flat to low single-digit top line. At AIS, memory costs will be about a couple of hundred basis points of gross margin impact over the year, mitigated by growth, so AIS operating profit margins are about flat or slightly growing while margin dollars keep rising. Longer term (CEO): ABL's growth algorithm is to enter new verticals, take share and grow with the market, adding around 50 to 100 basis points of adjusted operating profit margin per year; AIS focuses on organic and inorganic growth with margin expansion over time.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2027 net sales $4.7 billion to $4.9 billion; adjusted diluted EPS $20.50 to $22

quarterly_data.signal: Memory costs (CFO Karen Holcom): memory cost increases did not affect Q4 performance, but Acuity expects an impact on AIS margins in fiscal 2027 - on memory costs alone around a couple of hundred basis points of gross profit, partly offset by SG&A leverage as AIS grows. Priorities: first secure the inventory needed to service customers, second recover the incremental cost in dollars, then accelerate product and productivity initiatives to recover margins. CEO Neil Ashe: about 200 basis points of gross margin impact over the year, probably starting late in fiscal Q1 and into fiscal Q2 as the inventory works through sales; he called it 'just another one of those mild speed bumps'. At ABL (CEO): some inflation in commodities such as steel and freight, handled through purchasing, product development and manufacturing productivity; ABL's normal price increase was announced in September and goes live in December; ABL prices strategically for value and covers the dollar cost of supply shocks and trade-policy changes rather than pricing to a markup of inflation.
quarterly_data.figure: about 200 basis points AIS gross margin impact from memory costs in fiscal 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Data centers, CEO Neil Ashe: Acuity had 'a very strong year in data centers in '26 for lighting'; in Q4 ABL expanded the Lithonia Lighting BLT family with a purpose-built luminaire for data centers, designed around the specialized ceiling grid system these facilities use to simplify installation, and 'we'll continue to get our unfair share of data centers, on the lighting side.' In AIS: 'We have the premier DDC controller in the market at Distech, and we've added a PLC controller, which puts us in position to service multiple hyperscalers going forward'; existing sales continue and are growing, and 'we are in the door with more and more hyperscalers over time.'

ABL portfolio and position (CEO Neil Ashe): product vitality is core to ABL's strategy. New in the quarter: Luminis Hollowcore Element (broader applications and mounting options) and Ridge by Hydrel, a premium outdoor linear floodlight range for facades, bridges, tunnels and stadiums. At the controls layer nLight connects luminaires and sensors into one control architecture from a single room to an entire campus (wired and wireless), with SensorSwitch for simpler applications; at the components layer eldoLED Studio, a cloud-based application, configures, deploys, manages and updates LED drivers, used by the newly released Accela 85-watt driver with NFC. CEO: ABL is 'the undisputed leader in North America and the best-performing lighting company in the world' (company claim) and moved from high-30s to upper-middle-40s gross profit margins over the last 5 or 6 years through structural improvements. ABL order rates and the business climate have firmed and are expected to continue into next year; fiscal Q1 seasonality differs from normal only by last year's elevated backlog and the impact of corporate accounts. Growth in the independent sales network, which represents 80 independent markets across North America, indicates ABL is taking share.
quarterly_data.figure: Accela 85-watt driver; 80 independent markets in the independent sales network

quarterly_data.signal: AIS portfolio (CEO Neil Ashe): AIS has differentiated, growing portfolios in building operations and in experiences, and over time a common data architecture will enable interoperability across them. QSC completed its first full year as part of Acuity; in 2026 the focus was extending Q-SYS into new customer spaces, new solutions and multinational expansion. New Q-SYS offerings: network video management (NVM), the next generation of video distribution in Q-SYS, connecting and managing low-latency video across hundreds of endpoints (e.g. stadiums and casinos), and RoomSuite, the Collaboration Bar and the Scheduling Panel for small and medium-sized spaces. QSC, Distech and Atrius bring open-protocol technologies into a single data layer, and end users are starting to pull these solutions through the channel, which is how the revenue synergies will show. Acuity has a strong acquisition pipeline with multiple companies to choose from; the priority is growing Intelligent Spaces into a larger portion of the company.

FY2026 cash flow and capital allocation (CFO Karen Holcom): cash flow from operations $826 million, $225 million higher than fiscal 2025, from operating performance, tariff refunds and lower tax payments; capital expenditures $78 million. Acuity repaid $200 million of debt in fiscal 2026 and another $200 million after the year closed, fully repaying the borrowings used to finance the QSC acquisition; it increased the dividend by 18% and allocated $287 million to repurchase over 940,000 shares.
quarterly_data.figure: Cash flow from operations $826 million (+$225 million); capex $78 million; $200 million debt repaid in fiscal 2026 and $200 million after year-end

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Neil Ashe on AI: Acuity is building a 'human-agentic organization', redesigning core processes with agentic abilities and reimagined workflows and raising associate productivity through LLMs and agentic workflow development; AI is embedded in products such as Q-SYS Reflect and Atrius DataLab. He called himself an AI optimist and said the technology investments are purposeful; he expects the revenue impact to come over time as AI shortens product development life cycles and, at AIS, through AI applications that drive outcomes for customers in spaces.
